raw_response:
I farm only 4.1 mu, and I have been doing wheat-maize for many years, so I will keep the same system this year. I do not read books, but I know my land, and with only two people in the household, I will keep things steady and practical rather than risky. For wheat, I will stay with improved seed, use moderate fertilizer, irrigate a few key times with my well, and keep pesticide use limited to what is needed because wheat on my land responds best to stable management, not excessive input. After wheat harvest, I will plant maize on the same 4.1 mu and I will use hybrid seed because maize gives better yield that way; I will give it more nitrogen than wheat, irrigate when summer rain is not enough, and do a couple of pesticide sprays if insects or disease show up. I will use rotary tillage because it saves labor and suits my small farm. My goal is steady yield, controlled cost, and manageable work for my age and household size.
